To base this patch on top of the original 9275 fallocate patch, the easiest is to just add a second patch on the same branch and then push the second patch (taking care that the parent was not modified or refreshed, or it will cause the parent to be updated and restart build/test/review).

If it is someone else's patch (not the case here, but just FYI), use the "Download" menu on the top right of each patch and select "Checkout" to get an exact copy of that patch, and use "git checkout -b b_<branch_name>" to create a new branch to develop your new patch on. Then, when you push the second patch (taking care that the branch has not been rebased) Gerrit can see that the exact parent hash and Commit-Id is already present and will not create a separate patch for it.

Patch Set 6:

The main fallocate() patch is pretty much ready to land, it would be good to refresh this based on my previous review so that ZFS can also be included at the same time.

After that, having FALLOC_FL_PUNCH_HOLE and FALLOC_FL_ZERO_RANGE functions would be useful as well, and likely not much more than checking the features passing the flags through for ldiskfs.  PUNCH_HOLE will need some wiring for ZFS, since it already has this functionality, and I suspect that ZERO_RANGE would end up being the same as PUNCH_HOLE for ZFS, since "preallocating blocks" doesn't make sense since they cannot be overwritten in place.

I don't think the FALLOC_FL_COLLAPSE_RANGE and FALLOC_FL_INSERT_RANGE functions will be easy implement on Lustre, unless the file has only a single stripe and we could just pass the request down to ldiskfs, or the shift is a multiple of stripe_size * stripe_count.

The FALLOC_FL_UNSHARE_RANGE function doesn't make sense, since neither ldiskfs or ZFS allow clone_file_range().

We are only returning SUCCESS and FAILURE without doing any actual allocation for ZFS fallocate. The TC for ZFS calling fallcoate should not be checking for size and blocks as we are doing for ldiskfs. It should just be checking for file created, ENOSPC, EOPNOTSUPP and SUCCESS. 

We should be having other set of TC for ZFS which does the above minimal checks and not share it with ldiskfs TC for fallocate?

Please advice

Thanks

 > ldiskfs. It should just be checking for file created, ENOSPC,
 > EOPNOTSUPP and SUCCESS.
 > 
 > We should be having other set of TC for ZFS which does the above
 > minimal checks and not share it with ldiskfs TC for fallocate?

If there is common functionality in a subtest that applies to both backing filesystems, then the subtest could be used, maybe putting some checks under [ "$ost1_FSTYPE" = "ldiskfs" ] or similar.  It is fine to skip all of the checks for the reserved blocks for ZFS, and only check the file size (for KEEP_SIZE and not).

More interesting for ZFS is when the PUNCH_HOLE is wired up to fallocate(), since it can do that.  Also, fsx should still work regardless of whether ZFS is actually reserving space or not.

Patch Set 13:

Hi Andreas,

I saw your comment and wanted to reply early...but could not...sorry.

>I also see the same pattern of dropping oo_lock ...

You are correct. The reason could be that the API authors wanted to avoid holding a sleeping lock inside a spinning one. The calls looks like...

osd_object_sa_update()
	-> sa_update()
		-> mutex_enter(&hdl->sa_lock); //sleeping
	-> osd_object_sa_dirty_add()

Maybe this is the reason the authors dropped lock and re-take it under osd_object_sa_dirty_add() again.



> (minor) I wonder if it makes sense to hold oo_attr_lock across osd_object_sa_update() *IFF* we made a change to not get oo_attr_lock in osd_object_sa_dirty_add()?

Looks like we cannot as sa_update() is internally calling a mutex (sleeping) lock.

Thanks
Arshad

Patch Set 17: Code-Review+1

I updated the patch to avoid holding the spinlock over dmu_prealloc() that the Lustre Gerrit Janitor was complaining about.

That got me wondering exactly what the semantics of this function are, since there is no documentation for it in the ZFS source code, and Google turns up virtually nothing at all (even the one document in Russian doesn't help much).

I updated the prealloc test to verify that previously-written data is not clobbered by the prealloc call.  I'd _assume_ this is already tested by fsx in its various modes, but I don't know how often that calls fallocate() in the "no-clobber" preallocation mode, so it is possible that we've just gotten lucky?  I wonder if it makes sense to run a much longer fsx run to verify more correct behavior, or try the fallocate tests from xfstests, which are likely very comprehensive.

However, this patch needs to update test-framework.sh check_set_fallocate() and check_set_fallocate_or_skip() to allow the fallocate tests to run on ZFS.  Otherwise this could (potentially) crash on the first ZFS usage of fallocate and we wouldn't notice until it is out the door.

It looks like check_set_fallocate() needs to be updated to always set new_mode=1 for ZFS so that it actually consumes the OST space.  Most of the subtests calling fallocate depend on it consuming space for files and OSTs.  A few, like sanity.sh::test_150g are testing PUNCH, but also have a specific exclusion for ZFS (that should be moved after check_set_fallocate_or_skip so that the error message is more consistent), but there may be a few other places that need explicit checks.

As such, I don't think this patch should be marked "trivial" since fallocate is used in quite a number of different tests already (sanity, sanityn, sanity-quota, sanity-flr, ost-pools) that should all be tested with this change.
